fields.Participants: Solar Installer, Customer, Solar Sales Coordinator
fields.Trigger: Customer confirms interest in solar system purchase

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-schedule of "schedules site survey with certified installation partner within 5 business…" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-capture of "capture data into ERP" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-generate of "generates updated quotation with actual costs" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-440 (ensure controlled execution — Solar Installation Coordination & Permitting (PA-70.2).)
- operational: Solar Installation Partner review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Structural issues**: Older roofs may require reinforcement, adding PHP 20K–50K to project cost
- **Survey delays**: Limited installer capacity in provincial areas (Visayas, Mindanao)
System Touchpoints: - Mobile site survey app with photo capture and measurement logging
- Solar design tool integration with ERP product catalog
- Quotation update with site-specific cost adjustments
Time Estimate: - 2–3 hours on-site; 1–2 days for design and quotation

steps.activity: Solar Sales Coordinator schedules site survey with certified installation partner within 5 business days of lead qualification; provides customer brief with preliminary system sizing from in-store consultation

Installation partner conducts on-site assessment: roof structural integrity, orientation and tilt angle, shading analysis (trees, buildings), electrical panel capacity, meter location, conduit routing; takes photos and measurements; uses mobile app to capture data into ERP

Installer produces final system design: panel layout, inverter placement, cable routing, structural mounting requirements; generates updated quotation with actual costs (scaffolding, structural reinforcement, electrical upgrades if needed); Coordinator presents to customer for approval

fields.Participants: Solar Sales Coord, Installation Partner, Logistics, Store Ops

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-create of "creates installation work order in ERP" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-log of "Logistics arranges special delivery" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System rule-based auto-approval of "Installation partner arrives on-site, confirms material receipt and completeness" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-440 (ensure controlled execution — Solar Installation Coordination & Permitting (PA-70.2).)
- operational: Solar Sales Coordinator review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Weather delays**: Rainy season (Jun–Nov) delays rooftop installation work
- **Partner capacity**: Limited number of PRC-licensed installers (RA 7920) in provincial areas
System Touchpoints: - Installation work order management with partner assignment
- Delivery scheduling integration with installation timeline
- Mobile work order status updates with photo documentation

steps.activity: Coordinator confirms customer order and creates installation work order in ERP; assigns to installation partner based on geographic coverage, certification level (PRC-licensed Registered Master Electrician per RA 7920 required), and current workload; confirms installation date with customer (typically 2–4 weeks lead time)

Coordinator coordinates material delivery: generates pick list for store/DC, schedules delivery to customer site 1–2 days before installation, confirms installation partner has required tools and mounting hardware; Logistics arranges special delivery (panels require careful handling)

Installation partner arrives on-site, confirms material receipt and completeness, executes installation per approved design; updates work order status in mobile app with progress photos at key milestones (mounting, panel placement, inverter installation, wiring)

fields.Participants: Solar Sales Coord, Customer, DU (Distribution Utility), ERC
fields.Trigger: Solar system installation completed and passed inspection

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-document of "Coordinator prepares net metering application package" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-inspect of "inspection and meter change" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-export of "Upon DU approval and bi-directional meter installation" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-440 (ensure controlled execution — Solar Installation Coordination & Permitting (PA-70.2).)
- operational: Solar Sales Coordinator review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **DU processing delays**: Provincial DUs may take 8+ weeks for net metering approval
- **Application rejection**: Incomplete electrical diagrams or non-compliant installations require rework
System Touchpoints: - Net metering application tracking with DU-specific process templates
- Work order status with net metering stage
- Customer notification system for milestone updates
Time Estimate: - 30–120 min per occurrence; 2–8 weeks for DU processing

steps.activity: Coordinator prepares net metering application package: ERC certificate of compliance, electrical plan/diagram, installation photos, installer license, customer documents (ID, proof of ownership, DU account number); submits to DU per their specific process (Meralco online portal, provincial DU walk-in)

DU conducts inspection and meter change (bi-directional meter); Coordinator tracks application status; follows up with DU every 5 business days; manages customer expectations (DU processing: 2–8 weeks depending on utility)

Upon DU approval and bi-directional meter installation: Coordinator confirms net metering activation; customer begins earning export credits; Coordinator closes installation work order and triggers warranty registration (W2541)

fields.Participants: Quality Inspector, Solar Installer, Category Manager

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-inspect of "inspector" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-record of "records all test results in commissioning report via mobile app" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-schedule of "schedules re-inspection within 5 business days" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-440 (ensure controlled execution — Solar Installation Coordination & Permitting (PA-70.2).)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Electrical safety**: Improper wiring creates fire risk; mitigated by mandatory inspection
- **Inspector availability**: Limited qualified inspectors in provincial areas create bottleneck
System Touchpoints: - Commissioning checklist and test result recording via mobile app
- Work order stage progression (Installation → Commissioning → Net Metering)
- Punch list tracking for failed inspections

steps.activity: Quality Inspector (BuildRight or third-party) conducts commissioning inspection: verifies panel mounting torque, wiring compliance (Philippine Electrical Code), inverter installation, grounding system, DC/AC disconnect accessibility, label compliance, fire safety clearance

Inspector performs electrical testing: open-circuit voltage measurement per string, insulation resistance test, ground continuity test, inverter startup and grid synchronization; records all test results in commissioning report via mobile app

If passed: Inspector signs off commissioning certificate; triggers net metering application (W2536) and warranty registration (W2541). If failed: issues punch list to installer, schedules re-inspection within 5 business days

fields.Participants: Solar Sales Coord, Customer, LGU Building Official, Licensed Engineer

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-generate of "prepares LGU permit application" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-document of "Coordinator submits application to LGU Building Official" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-inspect of "inspection scheduled post-installation for final occupancy/electrical clearance" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-440 (ensure controlled execution — Solar Installation Coordination & Permitting (PA-70.2).)
- operational: Solar Sales Coordinator review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **LGU variability**: Each of the ~150 LGUs with BuildRight stores has different solar permit requirements and processing times
- **Engineer availability**: PEE sign-off required; limited PEEs in some provincial areas
System Touchpoints: - LGU permit tracking with jurisdiction-specific requirements
- Document management for permits and certifications
- Licensed engineer credential tracking
Time Estimate: - 30–120 min per occurrence; 5–15 days for LGU processing

steps.activity: Coordinator prepares LGU permit application: electrical plan signed by licensed Professional Electrical Engineer (PEE), structural certification for roof loading, building permit (if required by LGU for solar installations), fire safety clearance; requirements vary by LGU

Coordinator submits application to LGU Building Official; tracks approval timeline (typically 5–15 business days); coordinates with Licensed Electrical Engineer for any revisions or additional documentation requested

Upon permit approval: installation can proceed; LGU inspection scheduled post-installation for final occupancy/electrical clearance; Coordinator ensures all documentation archived in ERP for future reference and warranty claims

fields.Participants: Logistics Coord, Store/DC Ops, Installation Partner, Customer

workflows.name: Solar Installation Material Staging & Delivery Coordination

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "Logistics Coordinator picks and stages installation materials at originating…" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-schedule of "schedules special delivery" (replaces manual Step 2).
Controls: - operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Panel damage in transit**: ~2–3% breakage rate; requires careful handling and insurance
- **Site access**: Urban installations (Metro Manila) face parking and access restrictions
System Touchpoints: - Pick/pack with special handling instructions for solar components
- TMS with special vehicle requirements
- BOM-based delivery completeness check

steps.activity: Logistics Coordinator picks and stages installation materials at originating location (store or DC): panels (fragile), inverter, mounting rails, cables, connectors, breakers, conduits; creates consolidated shipment for site delivery

Coordinator schedules special delivery: panels require flat-bed or covered truck (no stacking); arranges delivery 1–2 days before installation; confirms customer site access (roof access, parking for truck, crane/hoist availability for 2+ story buildings)

Delivery executed; installation partner or customer signs goods receipt; Coordinator confirms material completeness vs. BOM; any missing items trigger emergency store-to-site replenishment within 24 hours

fields.Participants: Solar Sales Coord, DU Technician, Customer, Installer

workflows.name: Solar System Grid Connection & Net Metering Activation

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-sync of "DU technician visits customer site" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-file of "Coordinator confirms activation with customer" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-post of "posts revenue recognition" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **DU scheduling delays**: Bi-directional meter installation may take 4–8 weeks after application approval
- **Customer confusion**: Net metering billing complexity requires clear explanation
System Touchpoints: - Work order closure with revenue posting
- Warranty registration trigger
- CRM project completion with cross-sell opportunity flag

steps.activity: DU technician visits customer site: replaces existing unidirectional meter with bi-directional net meter; verifies system connection and grid synchronization; tests export power measurement

Coordinator confirms activation with customer: explains net metering billing mechanics (export credit calculation, monthly settlement, excess generation rollover); provides customer with monitoring app setup instructions; takes final system photos for project file

Coordinator closes project in ERP: completes installation work order, triggers warranty registration (W2541), posts revenue recognition (product sale + installation service), updates CRM with completed sale for future cross-sell (battery upgrade, EV charger)

fields.Participants: Solar Sales Coord, Customer, Vendor, Installation Partner

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-capture of "enters serial numbers, installation date, and contractor details into ERP…" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-log of "login for warranty claim submission" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-validate of "verify system performance" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-440 (ensure controlled execution — Solar Installation Coordination & Permitting (PA-70.2).)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Multi-vendor warranty complexity**: Panels, inverter, and installation each have different warranty terms and claim processes
- **Customer neglect**: Customers may not perform required maintenance, voiding performance warranties
System Touchpoints: - Warranty registration module with multi-vendor warranty tracking
- Customer portal for warranty claim submission
- CRM with maintenance reminder and upsell scheduling

steps.activity: Coordinator registers warranties: panel performance warranty (25-year linear, 12-year product), inverter warranty (5–10 years), battery warranty (5–10 years), installation workmanship warranty (2 years); enters serial numbers, installation date, and contractor details into ERP warranty module

Coordinator prepares customer handover package: system documentation (as-built diagram, equipment manuals, warranty certificates), maintenance guide (panel cleaning schedule, inverter monitoring, annual inspection), emergency contacts, ERP portal login for warranty claim submission

Coordinator schedules 6-month follow-up call to verify system performance; enters customer into annual maintenance reminder program; flags for upsell opportunities (battery storage, EV charger, system expansion) at 12-month mark
